fields.label: A
skills_required: Understanding of Harmonic-to-Noise Ratio computation via Praat/parselmouth — specifically what HNR measures in a singing voice vs a spoken voice, and why breathiness, creakiness, and modal phonation produce different HNR ranges

Knowledge of librosa.pyin's pitch confidence output — what the confidence value actually represents (probabilistic voicing decision vs tracking certainty), and under what conditions it collapses to near-zero even on a correctly-pitched signal

Understanding of spectral flatness as a voice quality metric — what flatness of 1.0 means (white noise), what causes a singing voice to read high flatness despite correct pitch, and whether Arabic consonantal density (ق, ع) would register as flatness spikes or pitch gaps
questions: The proposal treats HNR as 'the closest numerical proxy to vocals don't sound clear' — but HNR is computed on the isolated vocal stem after UVR5 separation. If the stem separator leaks instrumental bleed into the vocal stem (a known failure mode of BS-Roformer on dense low-mid content), will that bleed depress HNR in a way that is indistinguishable from a genuine vocal clarity problem?

The proposal assigns pitch confidence a dual role: low mean = pitch instability, high std dev = erratic. librosa.pyin returns a confidence array with a value per analysis frame, including frames classified as unvoiced. If unvoiced frames (consonants, breath gaps) are included in the mean and std dev, does the resulting statistic describe pitch quality or simply the ratio of voiced-to-unvoiced frames — and are these two interpretations separated anywhere in the proposed implementation?

The Vocal-to-Accompaniment Ratio (VAR) is described as RMS in the presence band (1k–4kHz) of vocal stem vs instrumental stem — but the existing _band_energy_fraction() in extractor.py returns a fraction of each stem's own total power, not an absolute RMS. Does a VAR computed from these fractional values produce a meaningful dB-style ratio, or does it require computing absolute RMS in the band on each stem independently before taking the ratio?

fields.label: B
skills_required: Understanding of the existing flat-dict data contract — extract_features() returns a single scalar per feature; profiler.analyze_chunk() consumes that dict and produces scalar deltas; scorer.score_chunk() iterates over those scalars against config.THRESHOLDS — the entire chain assumes one number per feature per file

Knowledge of what a windowed time-series output (Extension B's per-window CSV with columns [time_start, time_end, HNR, pitch_confidence, rms_vocal, spectral_flatness]) implies for the scorer and reporter: these are not scalars and cannot flow through the existing THRESHOLDS/WEIGHTS integrity check or the score_chunk() formula without a parallel or replacement code path

Familiarity with pre-processing stage injection — UVR5 stem separation must run before any feature extraction call; main.py currently calls _load_or_build_reference() and analyze_chunk() as the pipeline entry points, neither of which has a stem-separation hook, meaning the three-table output (full mix | vocal stem | instrumental stem) requires either a new orchestration layer or significant surgery to run_single() and run_style_compare()
questions: Extension A requires running the full metric suite on three signals (full mix, vocal_stem.wav, instrumental_stem.wav) and producing three parallel feature dicts. profiler.analyze_chunk() currently takes one chunk_path and one reference_profile and returns one delta dict. Does the proposal require three separate calls to analyze_chunk() — one per signal — and if so, does the reference profile for vocal_stem and instrumental_stem come from a pre-separated reference track (which must also be run through UVR5), or is there no per-stem reference and the three-table structure is a raw values table with no delta column for stems?

scorer.score_chunk() iterates over config.THRESHOLDS keys and reads deltas[feature] as a scalar. Extension B's windowed metrics (HNR per window, pitch confidence per window) are lists, not scalars. If these windowed features are added to the deltas dict, will scorer.py raise a TypeError when it calls abs(delta) on a list — and does the proposal explicitly exclude windowed features from the scoring formula, or does it assume a summary statistic (e.g. mean HNR) will be computed before the delta is handed to the scorer?

config.py enforces a strict key-alignment invariant at import time: every key in THRESHOLDS must exist in WEIGHTS and vice versa, or a ValueError is raised. Extension A proposes five new vocal-stem metrics (HNR, VAR, pitch_confidence, spectral_flatness, F0_range). If these are added to extractor.py's output and fed into the scoring pipeline, do they each require a new entry in both THRESHOLDS and WEIGHTS — and has the proposal specified any calibrated threshold values for them, or are they currently unanchored?
